title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-throughput-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated customer fleets have observed intermittent SLA misses during short high-traffic bursts and unclear accounting of burst consumption against committed throughput. This PR introduces a coordinated set of changes: 1) deterministic burst tokenbucket controls at the fleet autoscaler level to enforce short-duration throughput guarantees while protecting long-term capacity commitments, 2) a throughput guarantee enforcement path that preemptively throttles non-guaranteed routes when a fleet is near commit limits, and 3) enhanced utilization and burst consumption reporting surfaced to the Console and exported to telemetry pipelines. Summary of changes: - Add a fleet-level tokenbucket implementation that supports per-priority buckets, burst-credit accrual, and smoothing windows. - Integrate tokenbucket checks into the autoscaler decision path to enable graceful shedding before scaling events when burst budgets are exhausted. - Add a secondary fast-path that marks requests as "best-effort" when they would violate guaranteed throughput; those requests are now eligible for cheaper model fallbacks or delayed queuing. - Emit new metrics: dedicated.fleet.burst.available_tokens, dedicated.fleet.burst.consumed_tokens, dedicated.fleet.throughput.guarantee_violation, dedicated.fleet.utilization.commit_pct. - Add Console panels (fleet overview, burst budget timeline) and a CSV export for per-fleet daily burst usage. - Backfill e2e tests and unit tests for tokenbucket edgecases, plus a smoke test that verifies throughput guarantees under a synthetic burst workload. Backwards compatibility and deployment: All changes are behind a feature flag (autoscaler.burst_controls_v2) to enable gradual rollout. The new metrics are additive and will not change existing metric names. The autoscaler path falls back to the legacy behavior when the flag is disabled. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for tokenbucket logic - [x] Integration tests for autoscaler path - [x] Console changes reviewed by UX - [x] Telemetry export schema updated - [x] Feature flag gating and migration plan included Testing notes: Added a synthetic canary job that simulates 10s and 60s bursts across priorities; verified no long-term commit oversubscription and verified graceful shedding at headroom < 5%. Related: ENG-4523 (throughput guarantees), ENG-5120 (console burst UX).
commits: feat(autoscaler): add fleet-level tokenbucket with per-priority buckets
fix(autoscaler): handle negative token accrual edgecase in smoothing window
chore(console): add fleet burst panels and CSV export
test(autoscaler): add synthetic burst e2e canary test
docs: document autoscaler.burst_controls_v2 rollout and migration
files_changed: services/autoscaler/manager.go - add tokenbucket integration and new decision path
services/requests/router.go - mark requests as best-effort when needed
services/telemetry/metrics.go - new metric definitions and export hooks
code_snippet: // tokenbucket check in autoscaler decision path if flag enabled if cfg.FeatureFlag('autoscaler.burst_controls_v2') { if !fleet.TokenBucket.Allow(req.Priority, req.Tokens) { markBestEffort(req) } }
review_comments: Samir: Can we quantify the performance impact of tokenbucket checks on hot paths? Response: added microbenchmarks showing <0.5% latency p95 increase; tokenbucket is lock-free for reads in the common case.

Priya: What happens during autoscaler leader failover? Response: tokenbucket state is stored in the autoscaler leader-only in-memory cache and persisted to a compact snapshot in redis every 5s; follower takes over and loads last snapshot. Added extra durability tests.
Daniel: Console CSV export could be large for big fleets; can we paginate? Response: updated endpoint to stream CSV and added pagination parameters and server-side cutoffs.
QA(Alina): e2e flaked once on CI due to timing; added retries and tightened timeouts in synthetic canary.
merge_summary: Squash and merge by Samir Patel after approvals. Commit message normalized to 'feature(autoscaler): fleet burst controls + throughput reporting' and changelog entry added.
release_notes: Enhancement: Fleet autoscaler now supports managed burst tokenbuckets to provide short-duration throughput guarantees and improved utilization reporting. Controlled rollout via feature flag autoscaler.burst_controls_v2. Operators should review the new Console burst panels and the ops runbook at docs/ops/autoscaler-burst-controls.md.
